note: Knee OA pain: the rat MIA/MNX models that showed analgesia for TrkA inhibitors were followed by one failed (ASP7962), one modest 4-week (GZ389988A) and one abandoned (VM902A) Phase 2; no member was ever filed.
label: Osteoarthritis (TrkA)

engagement.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
engagement.note: Rat pain behaviour (weight-bearing, paw withdrawal) was the only PD readout; no member measured TrkA blockade in people.
engagement.short: Rat pain behaviour, no human PD
engagement.quote: Pain behaviour was assessed as weight-bearing asymmetry and paw withdrawal threshold to punctate stimulation.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); AR786 is a class proxy, not a member.
engagement.judgement: The published rat-MIA/MNX TrkA-inhibitor paper is for AR786, a sibling TrkA inhibitor outside the member list; allowed as the model side with product_in_model false. Sanofi's GZ389988 rat-MIA abstract (OARSI 2015) could not be located by Crossref or search, so the member's own preclinical record is unverified.

engagement.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
engagement.note: Neither ASP7962 nor GZ389988A trial measured TrkA engagement in participants; the editorial names this as the open question.
engagement.short: No target engagement in either trial
engagement.quote: Neither study directly confirmed target engagement in the study participants, and it is possible that the lower affinity of ASP7962 for TrkA, or the lipophilic nature of GZ389988A affected the extent of TrkA blockade.
engagement.confidence_note: Editorial full text read via PMC6941477 (author manuscript).
engagement.reason: No human engagement readout for any member
engagement.judgement: Stays untested: the only human PD translation for TrkA inhibition (PF-06273340 UVB pain, Loudon 2018) is a pan-Trk non-member and so does not score under v3; ONO-4474 (pan-Trk) is likewise excluded. The editorial is a peer-reviewed commentary with PMID, used here only for its statement that no member confirmed engagement.

dose.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
dose.note: Rat efficacy at 30 mg/kg BID oral; no plasma exposure target was published to carry into patients.
dose.short: Rat dose only, no exposure target
dose.quote: Oral doses (30 mg/kg) of AR786 or vehicle were administered twice daily in either preventive (day -1 to -27) or treatment (day 14-28) protocols.
dose.judgement: No member has a published preclinical exposure target: the ASP7962 and GZ389988A trial papers are CC-BY-NC-ND but the journal site blocked full-text retrieval, so whether Watt 2019 states that 100 mg BID met a rat-derived exposure could not be checked.

dose.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
dose.note: ASP7962 100 mg BID was set on preclinical and Phase 1 data; whether that exposure was enough is the editorial's open question, not a tested one.
dose.short: Dose adequacy left open after failure
dose.quote: A major question for the oral TrkA inhibitor formulation is whether, despite careful preclinical and Phase 1 studies, the investigators advanced the most effective dosing regimen for the Phase 2 trial.
dose.confidence_note: Editorial full text read; Watt 2019 full text (dose rationale, PK) not retrievable, abstract only.
dose.reason: No published exposure target to check
dose.judgement: Not scored contra-derived-from-efficacy because the v3 table needs the model's exposure target to have been reached in patients, and no published source for ASP7962 or GZ389988A states such a target or human PK against it. If Watt 2019 full text states that 100 mg BID met a preclinically defined exposure, this entry becomes contra with derived_from efficacy. ONO-4474's rat/monkey trough target (Ishiguro 2020) is a non-member and does not score. GZ389988A Part A escalation was PK/safety only (NCT02845271).

efficacy.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
efficacy.note: AR786 prevented and reversed weight-bearing asymmetry and allodynia in rat MIA and meniscal-transection knee OA.
efficacy.short: TrkA inhibitor relieves pain in rat OA
efficacy.quote: Blocking NGF activity by inhibiting TrkA reduced pain behaviour in two rat models of OA.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); AR786 is a class proxy, not a member.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the track at the first published TrkA-inhibitor rat OA paper (epub 2015-08-18). The members' own rat data (GZ389988 OARSI 2015 abstract; any ASP7962 or VM902A pharmacology) are unpublished or unlocated.

efficacy.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
efficacy.note: Rat OA promised analgesia; oral ASP7962 100 mg BID gave -0.14 vs placebo on WOMAC pain (NS) while naproxen gave -0.67.
efficacy.short: ASP7962 failed WOMAC pain despite rat OA
efficacy.quote: Four-week treatment with ASP7962 (100 mg BID) did not improve pain or physical function in individuals with painful knee osteoarthritis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Watt 2019 abstract-level (full text blocked); EudraCT 2014-004996-22 results first published 2018-06-20, which sets the year.
efficacy.reason: Rat OA analgesia; ASP7962 failed WOMAC
efficacy.judgement: contra rests on ASP7962 (member; Phase 2a, n=215, NCT02611466, primary WOMAC pain week 4 missed, naproxen positive control worked). The model side is the AR786 rat paper, so comparison_stated is false and product_in_model false. GZ389988A (member, NCT02845271) met its 4-week primary (-7.49 VAS, P<0.05) but not 12 weeks; the editorial attributes part of it to CSF1R affinity, injection-site inflammation unblinding and baseline imbalance, and one drug's contra beats another's same on the same track. VM902A (member, NCT02847702) was terminated by company decision after 75 subjects with no results. Magnitude left null: the trial effect was indistinguishable from zero, not reversed, and the rat and human endpoints share no common unit. Year 2018 from the registry posting; the tier 1 paper (2019) sets the status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: WOMAC pain change vs placebo at week 4 (-0.14, 90% CI -0.62 to 0.34) against rat weight-bearing reversal; no shared unit

patient_trials.quote: No significant difference was observed between ASP7962 and placebo in change from baseline to Week 4 in WOMAC pain subscale score (-0.14; 90% 2-sided CI: -0.62, 0.34; P = 0.316)
The primary efficacy endpoint was met with a between-group difference of -7.49 (VAS 0-100) on WOMAC A1 changes over 4 weeks (P < 0.05 favoring GZ389988A).

efficacy.model: Human NTRK1 loss-of-function (congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis, HSAN IV)
efficacy.note: Recessive NTRK1 mutations cause congenital insensitivity to pain, the lifelong human loss-of-function that makes TrkA the analgesic target.
efficacy.quote: Our findings strongly suggest that defects in TRKA cause CIPA and that the NGF-TRKA system has a crucial role in the development and function of the nociceptive reception as well as establishment of thermoregulation via sweating in humans.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 8696348); the genotype is a model of the target, not of osteoarthritis.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the human genetic track at gene identification. Both member trial papers use it as target rationale (Krupka 2019 ref 25 Mardy 1999; Watt 2019 discussion), so it is a model the class relied on, not a retrodiction.

efficacy.model: Human NTRK1 loss-of-function (congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis, HSAN IV)
efficacy.note: Watt sets the pain-insensitive genotype beside ASP7962's failed WOMAC primary and blames incomplete, short blockade; GZ389988A met its 4-week primary.
efficacy.quote: Individuals with mutations of the TrkA receptor, either in humans or in pre-clinical models, have insensitivity to pain, suggesting that TrkA is a valid analgesic target.
efficacy.confidence_note: Watt full text read (ScienceDirect). The genotype is a lifelong complete loss; ASP7962 gave 4 weeks of partial blockade (unbound trough 44 ng/mL, below the 155 nM TrkA IC50), so the comparison is weak by construction.
efficacy.judgement: contra, not untested: an admissible comparison exists because the trial paper itself puts the genotype beside its primary-endpoint failure (comparison_stated true), and the model's prediction (TrkA blockade relieves pain) did not hold for ASP7962 (WOMAC pain -0.14 vs placebo, NS; naproxen -0.67). Watt attributes the gap to the degree and duration of blockade, recorded as source_calls_it scaling. GZ389988A (Krupka 2019, intro ref 25 cites the same genotype) met its 4-week primary, a same on this track, but one drug's contra beats another's same. Alternative reading for rule question 3: the genotype's condition (complete loss) was never produced by a member, which would make this untested; left to the checker. No dose entry: a genotype states no exposure target. Year 2019: the comparison first became public in Watt (epub 2019-07-26), not at the 2018-06-20 EudraCT posting, which carried no model.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: WOMAC pain change vs placebo at week 4 (-0.14, 90% CI -0.62 to 0.34) against lifelong pain insensitivity; no shared unit

patient_trials.quote: Four-week treatment with ASP7962 (100 mg BID) did not improve pain or physical function in individuals with painful knee osteoarthritis.
Human genetic mutations of TrkA are linked to congenital pain insensitivity.

efficacy.note: Trk-null mice lose trigeminal, sympathetic and dorsal-root ganglion neurons and die within a month: the pre-clinical TrkA loss-of-function.
efficacy.quote: Mice lacking Trk have severe sensory and sympathetic neuropathies and most die within one month of birth.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 8145823). The pain phenotype is stated by Indo 1996: these mice 'share dramatic phenotypic features of CIPA, including loss of responses to painful stimuli'.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the mouse genetic track at the knockout paper. A developmental null, not a pharmacological model: it predicts the target, not a dose.

efficacy.note: Watt's 'pre-clinical models' with TrkA mutations are the TrkA-null mice; placed beside ASP7962's failure with a blockade-degree excuse.
efficacy.quote: Individuals with mutations of the TrkA receptor, either in humans or in pre-clinical models, have insensitivity to pain, suggesting that TrkA is a valid analgesic target.
efficacy.confidence_note: Watt full text read; the sentence names 'pre-clinical models' without a reference, so the TrkA-null mouse is inferred (it is the only TrkA-mutant model with pain insensitivity, per Indo 1996).
efficacy.reason: Knockout pain loss; ASP7962 no analgesia
efficacy.judgement: Same comparison as the human genetic track, scored on its own model_id because a mouse null is a different system. contra with source_calls_it scaling (Watt: more complete, longer blockade by a mAb may be needed). Low confidence for two reasons: the model identity is inferred from Watt's wording, and a lethal developmental null is at best a target-validity statement. GZ389988A's 4-week success is subordinate. Rule question 3 applies as for the human genotype.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: WOMAC pain change vs placebo at week 4 (-0.14, NS) against knockout loss of nociceptive responses; no shared unit

patient_trials.quote: Four-week treatment with ASP7962 (100 mg BID) did not improve pain or physical function in individuals with painful knee osteoarthritis.

efficacy.note: p75-null mice still develop NGF hyperalgesia, so TrkA alone carries NGF's acute pain action: a TrkA-selective block should suffice.
efficacy.short: p75-null mouse: TrkA suffices for NGF pain
efficacy.quote: This means that NGF-induced hyperalgesia can occur in the absence of the p75 receptor and suggests that the trkA receptor is sufficient to mediate the acute noxious action of NGF.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 9835221). Watt 2019 ref 7, cited for 'p75NTR-knockout mice show similar NGF-induced hyperalgesia to wild-type mice'.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the track at the knockout paper. The prediction it carries for this class is that selective TrkA inhibition reproduces anti-NGF analgesia; it is a mechanism model, not a disease model.

efficacy.note: Watt rejects the 'mAb blocks more completely' excuse on this knockout evidence, leaving ASP7962's failure unexplained by the model.
efficacy.short: Knockout says TrkA block enough; it wasn't
efficacy.quote: However, this is not supported by pre-clinical evidence from NGF receptor knockouts.
efficacy.confidence_note: Watt full text read; the quoted sentence carries reference 7 (Bergmann 1998). The knockout answers whether TrkA is sufficient for NGF hyperalgesia, not whether a 4-week oral inhibitor relieves OA pain.
efficacy.judgement: The trial paper puts the knockout beside its own result as the reason the incomplete-blockade explanation fails, so comparison_stated true. The model's prediction, that TrkA-selective inhibition should match anti-NGF analgesia, did not hold for ASP7962 at plasma levels Watt calls above the IC50; Watt leaves it unresolved (source_calls_it unresolved). Low confidence: one sentence, mechanistic inference rather than a disease-model prediction. Its own track because it is a different mouse from the TrkA null.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: WOMAC pain change vs placebo at week 4 (-0.14, NS) against NGF-evoked hyperalgesia preserved without p75; no shared unit

patient_trials.quote: Four-week treatment with ASP7962 (100 mg BID) did not improve pain or physical function in individuals with painful knee osteoarthritis.

efficacy.model: Rat PGPS knee arthritis flare (GZ389988, single intra-articular dose)
efficacy.note: Single IA GZ389988 improved gait scores after PGPS-triggered painful flares; the member's second rat pain model besides MIA.
efficacy.short: IA GZ389988 relieves rat flare pain
efficacy.quote: GZ389988 was also efficacious in the PGPS arthritis model, demonstrating a significant improvement of gait analysis scores following painful disease reactivation flares (Fig. 2).
efficacy.confidence_note: OARSI 2015 congress abstract in a journal supplement (DOI, no PMID); no group sizes, doses or statistics beyond 'significant'. Full abstract read on ScienceDirect.
efficacy.judgement: Its own track: a streptococcal PGPS arthritis-flare model (Bolder BioPATH) is a different system from MIA knee OA, read by gait score after IV reactivation. Sponsor's own model, product_in_model true. Tier 1 is a stretch for a congress abstract; recorded with the caveat.

efficacy.model: Rat PGPS knee arthritis flare (GZ389988, single intra-articular dose)
efficacy.note: Krupka restates the rat relief of local knee pain, then meets the 4-week WOMAC A1 primary (-7.49/100); the 12-week secondary missed.
efficacy.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was met with a between-group difference of −7.49 (VAS 0–100) on WOMAC A1 changes over 4 weeks (P < 0.05 favoring GZ389988A).
efficacy.confidence_note: Krupka full text read. The rat side is stated in the same paper ('In rat models of OA and joint pain, GZ389988 showed a significant relief of local knee pain', ref 28 Flannery). Single-centre, n=104, one-sided alpha 0.05; suspension visibly differed from placebo; 12-week WOMAC A1 -6.78 (P=0.064).
efficacy.reason: Rat flare analgesia; GZ389988A met primary
efficacy.judgement: same at direction_only: the only member run in this model relieved knee pain in rats and met its pre-specified 4-week primary in patients. comparison_stated true because Krupka states the rat result in its own text rather than merely citing Flannery. Not neg: the rat effect was reported as significant, not sub-threshold. Weaknesses kept in confidence: the flare model is arthritis, not OA; the editorial (Walsh 2019) raises unblinding by appearance, baseline imbalance and CSF1R affinity. ASP7962 was never run in PGPS, so no contra competes on this track. registry_date null: NCT02845271 has no posted results (CT.gov checked 2026-11-05) and Krupka lists no EudraCT number.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: rat gait score after PGPS flare against WOMAC A1 -7.49/100 vs placebo at 4 weeks; no shared unit

patient_trials.quote: The secondary outcome on WOMAC A1 changes over 12 weeks had a between-group difference of −6.78 (P = 0.064).

safety.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
safety.note: Rat TrkA inhibition reduced synovitis and left osteochondral pathology unchanged; silent on the anti-NGF rapidly-progressive-OA liability.
safety.short: Rat joints unchanged by TrkA block
safety.quote: AR786 treatment reduced MIA-induced synovitis and did not significantly affect osteochondral pathology in either model.
safety.judgement: Opens the rat OA track on safety: 28-day joint histology, no joint harm predicted.

safety.model: Rat MIA and MNX knee OA (AR786, sibling TrkA inhibitor)
safety.note: No RPOA in either member trial, but exposures were 4 wk oral or one IA dose with RPOA-risk patients excluded, so the rat silence was never tested.
safety.quote: Rodent models have not convincingly replicated human RPOA associated with NGF blockade, so it is not possible to exclude this potential toxicity by preclinical testing of TrkA inhibitors.
safety.confidence_note: Editorial full text read; Krupka 2019 abstract-level.
safety.judgement: Stays untested rather than contra: all three member registry records (NCT02611466, NCT02845271, NCT02847702) exclude RPOA history or risk, GZ389988A screened by MRI, and follow-up was at most 24 weeks, so the rat model's silence on RPOA met no patient test. A contra reading on GZ389988A's injection-joint inflammation (two thirds of participants per the editorial, none on placebo) was rejected because the GZ389988 rat intra-articular abstract could not be read to confirm the model reported no local reaction. The single tibial-plateau stress fracture is recorded, not scored.

safety.note: Rat GLP studies predicted reversible sympathetic-ganglion atrophy with no functional deficit; ASP7962 patients over 4 weeks showed no sensory or autonomic harm.
safety.short: No neural dysfunction, rat or patient
safety.quote: ASP7962 did not cause any detectable dysfunction of the sympathetic and sensory nervous system in either study.
safety.confidence_note: Both sides abstract-level (Kigami paywalled; Watt full text blocked). The trial reports only 'safe and well-tolerated' over 4 weeks with no autonomic testing; the rat ran 13 weeks.
safety.reason: Rat neurotox prediction held over 4 wk
safety.judgement: A paired comparison I made: the model's stated prediction (reversible neuronal atrophy without dysfunction) held in the one member trial that dosed the same drug (Watt 2019: 'ASP7962 was safe and well-tolerated', AEs at naproxen-like frequency). Scored same at direction_only and low confidence because the 4-week trial is a weak test of a 13-week rat finding. Not a retrodiction: GLP 4-/13-week repeat-dose studies are IND-enabling and precede a Phase 2, though the 2021 abstract gives no study dates, so model_first_use_year is null. Published 2021 sets the year. Its own track because it is a different system from the rat OA pain model.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence or absence of sensory/autonomic dysfunction

safety.note: IA GZ389988 into rat knees: no body-weight, clinical or joint histopathologic change; the programme's only stated local-tolerability result.
safety.quote: In vivo biocompatibility studies with GZ389988 showed neither a treatment effect on body weight or clinical appearance, nor any significant histopathologic changes in joint tissues.
safety.confidence_note: OARSI 2015 congress abstract; dose, formulation, timepoint and group size of the biocompatibility study are not given.
safety.judgement: Its own track rather than the rat-MIA track: a tolerability study in undiseased knees asks a different question from the OA pain model (rule question 4 in the check file). If the checker's proposed contra on the rat-MIA safety cell is adopted instead, this track duplicates it and one should be dropped.

safety.note: Injection-joint inflammatory reaction in 67.3% of GZ389988A knees, none on placebo; transient, called a foreign-particle innate response.
safety.short: Rat silent; two-thirds got joint inflammation
safety.quote: The most frequent TEAEs were injection joint inflammatory reaction (IJIR). It occurred in 67.3% of subjects treated with GZ389988A but none in the placebo arm.
safety.confidence_note: Krupka full text read; Flannery abstract gives no histology timepoint, so a reaction lasting hours could have been missed by design rather than mispredicted. Krupka attributes the IJIR to particles (hsCRP rise, neutrophil/monocyte increase), not to TrkA.
safety.judgement: A paired comparison I made (Krupka does not mention the rat study): the model's stated prediction was no joint-tissue change after IA GZ389988, and the one patient trial of the same product showed an acute inflammatory reaction in two thirds of injected knees versus none on placebo, a harm a rat knee can show. Scored contra at low confidence. Rule question 2 (formulation harm vs on-target) is open; if read as a formulation harm it stays on this track as a platform harm. magnitude null: presence/absence, no number on the rat side.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence of injection-joint inflammatory reaction (67.3% vs 0%) against rat joint histology without change
